children: Americans felt the burn at the pump this August as surging energy costs from the Middle East conflict continued to drive inflation, even as prices for groceries and clothing flatlined, according to the Consumer Price Index report published on Friday.
Overall, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that

in August vs. +0.4% consensus and 0.1% growth recorded in the prior month. The core measure, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% M/M in August vs. +0.2% consensus and 0.2% growth seen in the previous month.

Energy-related categories completely dominated the list of highest M/M increases. Fuel oil saw a staggering 10.1% spike, followed by energy commodities at 4.2%, motor fuel at 4.1% and gasoline (all types) at 3.9%.
Beyond the energy sector, airline fares rose 2.7% from a month ago.

Conversely, the data revealed widespread stability across many core categories. Numerous key expenditure items, including apparel, food at home, cereals, new vehicles and used vehicles, all registered exactly 0.0% change for the month.
Providing some relief, utility (piped) gas service fell 1.1%, leading a small group of decliners that also included a 0.8% drop in motor vehicle insurance.

title: Energy up, groceries flat: Inside the August CPI report
